A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAEE. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, algorithms, tables and figures support a reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v2 reports original accuracy, latency, exit-layer and database-cost measurements, together with ablations and fine-tuning comparisons.

after.justification: v3 reports original classification results and analyses, plus summarization experiments using an out-of-domain retrieval database and new exit-layer distributions.

M1.justification: Database construction, top-k retrieval, distance weighting, probability filtering and earliest-maximizing-layer selection remain unchanged. Algorithms B.1–B.2 in v2 match C.1–C.2 in v3; the new task preparation and implementation explanations do not establish a changed RAEE algorithm.

E1.justification: The eight original classification/judgment tasks remain. v3 adds CNN/DailyMail and XSum summarization using a WikiText-2-v1 retrieval database, extending coverage to generation and mismatched retrieval/evaluation domains (Section 4.5 and Appendix F).

E2.justification: v3 removes DistilBERT and DistilRoBERTa from the main comparisons and drops v2's fine-tuned CALM/FREE comparisons. It adds AdaInfer comparisons on T5, Llama and Gemma, SLEB on Gemma, and HashEE/AdaInfer building-cost comparisons where v2 reported RAEE alone.

E3.justification: SLEB's removal budget changes from four Llama blocks to approximately 60% of layers, and the correct-only-database ablation changes backbone from RoBERTa-Large to Llama-3-8B. Timing hardware changes from RTX5000/A100-80GB to RTX4090/A100-40GB. New summarization experiments introduce next-token retrieval-data preparation and ROUGE-L evaluation; v2's one-epoch fine-tuning comparison is removed.

E4.justification: v3 adds analysis of potentially correctable full-model errors (Figure 1b), an out-of-domain retrieval test, and task-specific exit-layer distributions (Appendix H). The correct-only-database ablation is revised using Llama. The top-k and database-size ablation questions and the two retrieved-example case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained neighbor boxplots and added exit-frequency plots characterize behavior across examples rather than introducing performance-uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous accuracy, latency, ablation and exit-layer entries change. For example, RAEE-Llama's reported average score changes from 58.52 to 57.39 and average layer usage from 27.91 to 13.43. v3 Table 5 adds summarization ROUGE-L results of 14.01/7.15 versus the backbone's 8.95/5.22. Removed comparisons also remove results; partly changed settings preclude interpreting these revisions as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and exit-selection reasoning are retained. v3 factors the existing inner sum into S_i and renumbers equations, without adding or revising a theorem, proof or substantive mathematical property.

C1.justification: v3 drops the abstract's explicit zero-shot characterization and foregrounds corrective intermediate-layer information in the abstract and contributions. This is a limited reframing: v2 already claimed simultaneous acceleration and performance improvement and explained error correction in Section 4.3.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies acceleration by backbone size, adds interpretations of out-of-domain effectiveness and links exit distributions to latency. Conversely, it removes v2's explicit build-cost/generalization and retriever-quality limitations, along with discussion of stronger fine-tuned alternatives. The underlying error-correction explanation is retained rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies tau=0.9, supplies T5/Llama/Gemma prompts and label mappings, explains WikiText sentence/window preparation, and documents the forward-function exit implementation. It replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository link. Database-entry counts and optional parallel-execution guidance disappear. Newly disclosed prompts and tau do not establish that those settings changed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds CeeBERT, JEI-DNN, PALBERT, risk-controlled exits and newer vision/multimodal work, alongside citations supporting the new datasets. The central positioning against classifier-based exits and conventional retrieval augmentation remains. Moving related work from Appendix H to Section 5 is structural.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and motivation are substantially rewritten around two observations. Related work and building-cost discussion move into the main text, separate ablation sections are merged, and the appendices are reorganized with additions and removals. Terminology changes throughout from early exiting to early exit.

P2.justification: The framework diagram is redrawn, one motivational example is replaced by correctness bars, and latency plots receive new grouping, legends, colors and scales. Tables are reorganized by backbone; summarization and prompt tables and sixteen exit-distribution panels are added. Fine-tuning tables disappear, and eight latency panels become four selected-task panels.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves empirical support and reproducibility through the retrieval-domain-shift summarization test, broader backbone-specific comparisons, and previously missing threshold and prompt details. These gains are tempered by removal of useful fine-tuning comparisons and explicit retrieval limitations. Changed experimental settings also prevent treating refreshed timings as direct evidence of methodological improvement.
